content.text:
View A represents a yellow circle at the upper location that is currently dominating attention and is readily available for access. The other three locations hold a blue cross at right, a red square at lower, and a green triangle at left; these are much less likely to be selected now and are progressively harder to recover after one or two steps without resampling. Predicted responses to different selection commands mostly preserve the currently attended location (each command tends to keep selection where it already is), so the system has little effective control to reallocate attention away from the upper item in this view.

View B represents a red square at upper, a yellow triangle at right, a green cross at lower, and a blue circle at left; attention is currently concentrated on the left blue circle and is readily available. The other items are less likely to be accessed now and become less available after one and two steps. Most command choices in this view tend to converge attention onto the upper item, so while you can redirect attention away from the current left item, the system mainly drives selection toward the upper location rather than offering flexible alternative allocations.
